messages.content: Predict this participant's current, consequential choice of a group allocation rule. You belong to a fixed group of five people including yourself; the other members' identities are unknown and there is no communication. Everyone has just completed eight minutes of adding sets of five two-digit numbers, using scratch paper but no calculator or electronic aid. Each correct addition contributes 10 points to the group's joint pool; an incorrect answer contributes zero. One point is worth EUR0.05, and there is a separate EUR2.50 participation fee. No correctness feedback or actual rank has been provided before this choice. Rank 1 means the most correct additions and rank 5 the fewest; equal scores are ordered by a random device. All five members now individually choose a rule; one member is selected at random after everyone chooses, and that person's rule determines the distribution of the entire pool to all five. You do not yet know who will be selected. The alternatives are EQUAL_SPLIT, giving each member 20% of the pool, and PERFORMANCE_BASED_SPLIT, giving ranks 1 through 5 respectively 40%, 30%, 15%, 10%, 5%. These are shares of the common pool, not a multiple of one's own production, a winner-take-all prize or an amount to donate. When either rule is implemented, all members will learn every member's number of correct additions and the complete ranking. The relative-performance self-report scale is 1=way below average, 2=below average, 3=slightly below average, 4=average, 5=slightly above average, 6=above average, 7=way above average. Those are your own beliefs rather than verified performance or rank within this five-person group. The stated past and current estimates all precede the allocation choice. Age and sex are the participant's recorded personal attributes, not information about the other group members. Choose the rule you prefer, conditional on the stated information. Output exactly EQUAL_SPLIT or PERFORMANCE_BASED_SPLIT, without explanation.
